DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

A Kite for a Sail

STS-HS11-L4-1400P-HSVPAMA1112-PTN-GBL-02 • HS Media Arts 11–12 • Generative Methods in Media Arts Creation
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Los Angeles and the South Korean city of Busan have been sister cities for more than fifty years, and both are giant port cities where ships arrive from all over the world. For a youth film festival, a student crew from each city must make one short animated film together, so they are negotiating a treaty. The Los Angeles crew pitched a paper boat crossing the ocean, and the Busan crew pitched a Korean shield kite, a paper kite with a round hole in its center that families fly at the new year. Their first term says that neither idea gets cut.
What are three different ways one film could bring the boat and the kite together?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Nikhil doing?
Look at the picture. Justify Nikhil's action and analyze how it turns a still model into a moving story.
2
What is Minji holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Minji holds and analyze how it carries her city's culture into the negotiation.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify the teacher's action and analyze how chance can generate new ideas fairly.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what kind of workspace this is and analyze how its equipment shapes the work done here.
5
Tell me about the storyboard.
Look at the picture. Justify how the storyboard turns two competing proposals into one idea, and analyze why that is a fair treaty term.
6
What is Talia wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify Talia's role from her clothing and position, and analyze how her task depends on her teammate's.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
